sources.title: Rate of de novo mutations and the importance of father's age to disease risk
sources.access_status: Bibliographic record and headline quantitative findings confirmed by web search 2026-09-05; publisher full text not re-read in this session.
supports: Whole-genome sequencing of 78 Icelandic parent-offspring trios
Average de novo mutation rate 1.20e-8 per nucleotide per generation at mean paternal age 29.7
Approximately two additional de novo mutations per year of paternal age
does_not_establish: Any per-locus mutation probability used in this section
That the affine age model proposed here is the correct functional form
Any implemented result in this repository

sources.title: Parental influence on human germline de novo mutations in 1,548 trios from Iceland
sources.access_status: Bibliographic record and headline quantitative findings confirmed by web search 2026-09-05; publisher full text not re-read in this session.
supports: 1,548 parent-offspring trios and 108,778 high-quality de novo mutations
Mean 70.3 de novo mutations per trio
Maternal slope 0.37 and paternal slope 1.51 de novo mutations per year of parental age
does_not_establish: Transferability of Icelandic slopes to other populations
Locus-specific mutation probabilities
Any implemented result in this repository

sources.title: Tissue-specific mutation accumulation in human adult stem cells during life
sources.access_status: Bibliographic record and headline quantitative findings confirmed by web search 2026-09-05; publisher full text not re-read in this session.
supports: Adult stem cells of liver, colon and small intestine accumulate mutations throughout life
Approximately 40 novel mutations per year, approximately linear in age
Tissue-specific mutation spectra despite similar accumulation rates
does_not_establish: That somatic accumulation is exactly linear at all ages or in all tissues
Any link between somatic burden and an inherited phenotype prediction
Any implemented result in this repository

sources.title: The Age Distribution of Cancer and a Multi-stage Theory of Carcinogenesis
sources.access_status: Bibliographic record and headline findings confirmed by web search 2026-09-05; full text not re-read in this session.
supports: Multistage model in which incidence rises as a power of age

does_not_establish: That the multistage form applies to the Mendelian loci modelled in this paper

Any implemented result in this repository
